newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-KASHIMA ANTLERS WRAP UP J-LEAGUE FIRST STAG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KASHIMA ANTLERS WRAP UP J-LEAGUE FIRST STAG.

text.p: Brazilian forward Mazinho's sole early goal gave defending J-League champion Kashima Antlers on Saturday night the first-stage title in the 1997 season.
Kashima's 1-0 away win over Cerezo Osaka was a triumph for Brazilian-style football in Japan as the team has Zico as its technical director and fellow Brazilian Joao Carlos as manager.
Mazinho knocked home a rebound off Cerezo's goalkeeper in the 15th minute following a shot from Yasuo Manaka, who met a cross from Japanese international defender Naoki Soma.

The victory on the final day of first-stage action lifted Kashima to 37 points from 16 matches -- out of the reach of second-placed Yokohama Flugels, who finished two points behind the Antlers with a hard-fought 3-2 win at Hiroshima.
"I'm happy to see our long-term team plans produce this result. Every player had greater confidence from last year's league title and that was the key to our victory," Zico said.

Kashima had to endure relentless pressure from the home side for the final 30 minutes after news came in that the Flugels had turned a 2-0 half-time deficit into a 3-2 win after an injury-time header by Brazilian striker Valber.
First-stage title holder Kashima will meet the second-stage winner in the two-leg championship series in December to determine this season's overall league trophy winner.
The Antlers will be confirmed as overall league winner without a playoff match if it also wins the second stage which starts on July 30.
Kashima won the 1993 first stage in the J-League's inaugural season but lost the overall crown to second-stage winner Kawasaki in the playoff.
Kashima claimed its first league title last year, when the league competition was contested in just a one-stage format.
